exposure: deletion of the paternal copy of 15q11-q13
PWS genetic subtypes (deletion, UPD, imprinting defect)
cohort: 355 patients with Prader-Willi syndrome (PWS) from the Rare Diseases Clinical Research Network PWS registry
finding: Patients with PWS had a higher rate of perinatal complications compared with the general population, with no significant differences observed between genetic subtypes except for higher maternal age and pre-pregnancy weight in the UPD subgroup.
mod_finding: Caesarean section rate was higher in the PWS cohort (54%) compared to the general population (32%).
birth_weight: Low birth weight in 34% of PWS cohort
